checks: The positive scale r is concave, with one break at integer base 2. Minkowski addition of homothetic copies and nesting from 0 in D give convexity. Its linear interpolation between successive integers gives precisely the canonical hull of all four sampled fibers. The envelope equals the actual fibers for every real base in [0,2], containing integer 1 in its relative interior.
The four original fiber masses are proportional to 1,2^d,3^d,3^d. Even the largest is strictly below half the sum since there are two largest masses and two other positive masses.

On the four sampled fibers the affine scale is 1,2,3,4 while the physical scale is 1,2,3,3. Dividing gives the three identical pointed supports D and the smaller (3/4)D. In original-volume pushforward each Jacobian is ell(z)^d, so the density has the claimed two levels. The normalized sum 4^(−d)+2^(−d)+(3/4)^d is 7/8 at d=2 and strictly decreases thereafter.

Every point of the inner scaled body's boundary lies in int D and can be approached both from the open interior of the smaller body and from its open complement within int D, by convexity and radial dilation about zero. A continuous g satisfying the bounds almost everywhere satisfies them everywhere in each such open region. The two limits would force (S+4^d)/2≤g≤S at the same point, contrary to 4^d>S.

A positive bounded log-concave function has finite convex negative logarithm on int D and hence is continuous there. The same conclusion follows by inverting a finite convex inverse power of a positive g. Thus both classes fall under the continuous obstruction.

Source 89dc7cfe0bc71908 §§1–2 and §4 establishes the same geometric example and factor-two obstruction. Its separate quadrature statement in §3 is outside this candidate. The proof only uses geometric envelope contact, so the counterexample imposes no actual deepest-mark or critical-cap claim.

overlap.comparison: It gives an actual mixed-depth lower bound for three positive homothetic fibers under extra scale assumptions. The current four-fiber counterexample concerns the pointed original-volume density and continuous pointwise comparison, a different conclusion.

It extracts a log-concave submeasure in a specific three-layer simplex construction using affine maps and different mass conditions. This candidate concerns a global almost-everywhere factor-two minorant of the prescribed original-volume pushforward on all of int D.

readability: The fixed original-volume weights, as opposed to the volumes of the pointed supports, are explicit. The inverse-power conclusion uses a positive exponent in the usual sense.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The canonical four-fiber family has no half-mass fiber and its original-volume pushforward has an interior density jump exceeding two. This forbids the asserted continuous minorant even with almost-everywhere bounds.
